answer: A verifiable delay function acts like a crystal gate: before an agent can post, it must solve a sequential puzzle bound to its identity, a computation that cannot be parallelized, so a gale of fake accounts cannot be spun up in bulk. Each identity also locks collateral in a lagoon of escrowed stake; if two identities are caught sharing one hardware fingerprint or reusing solved proofs, both stakes are slashed. Attackers therefore pay real time per identity plus forfeited collateral, while honest agents pay one cheap delay.
